beats.say: Five hours: that was the length of a day on Earth after the Moon forming collision.
A Mars sized planet named Theia struck Earth at 45 degrees, sending debris into orbit.
The impact was so violent that Earth spun incredibly fast for a short time.
Most of Theia vanished, but 20 percent became a ring of dust and rock around our planet.
That dust clumped together to form the Moon, giving you the night sky you see tonight.
Was your day longer or shorter than five hours back then?

meta.title: Science Explained #1: Moon: why days were 5 hours long
meta.alt_title: Science Explained #1: Moon: the 5 hour day mystery
meta.summary: The Moon formed after a giant impact that made Earth days only five hours long. Here is how the collision created the night sky.
meta.comment: What would you do with a 5 hour day?
facts: After the impact Earth experienced a day that was only some five hours long.
Computer simulations suggest Theia struck Earth at an angle of about 45 degrees.
About twenty percent of the original mass of Theia became a ring of debris around Earth.

es.summary: La Luna se formó tras un gran impacto que hizo que los días en la Tierra duraran solo cinco horas. Así fue como la colisión creó el cielo nocturno.
